nca92b34f5d0.s: In which year was the Civil Disobedience Movement withdrawn?
nca92b34f5d0.x: The CDM was withdrawn in 1934, after the Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931) and the Communal Award and Poona Pact (1932).

nab7318355a1.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Second Round Table Conference (1931)?
o: V.V. Jogayya Pantulu went to assist Gandhi
Konda Venkatappayya went to assist Gandhi
A resolution for a separate Andhra was handed to Gandhi there
nab7318355a1.x: V.V. Jogayya Pantulu, not Konda Venkatappayya, went to RTC-2 to assist Gandhi and handed him the separate-Andhra resolution.

new.s: When did the Simon Commission arrive in India?
new.x: The Simon Commission was appointed in November 1927 and arrived on 3 February 1928.

new.s: The Calcutta session of the Congress (1928) accepted the Nehru Report with:
o: A one-year ultimatum to the British
A boycott of the Simon Commission only
A call for the Dandi March
new.x: Calcutta 1928 gave a one-year ultimatum; Purna Swaraj was adopted only at Lahore in 1929.

new.s: Who was the Viceroy during the Simon Commission visit, the Lahore Purna Swaraj session and the Dandi March?
new.x: Lord Irwin (1926-31) was Viceroy through all three events.

new.s: The distance covered by Gandhi in the Dandi March was about:
new.x: The march covered about 240 miles (385 km) in 24 days - not 240 km.

new.s: Dandi, where Gandhi broke the salt law, is in which district of Gujarat?
new.x: Dandi lies on the Gujarat coast in Navsari district.

new.s: How many days did the Dandi March from Sabarmati to Dandi take?
new.x: The march took 24 days; 78 is the number of followers.

new.s: Who compared the Dandi March to "Napoleon's return from Elba"?
new.x: Subhas Bose likened the Dandi March to Napoleon's march from Elba to Paris.

new.s: After his arrest on 5 May 1930, Gandhi was lodged in:
new.x: Gandhi was arrested on 5 May 1930 and taken to Yerwada Jail.

new.s: Who led the salt march from Trichinopoly to Vedaranyam in 1930?
new.x: Rajaji led the Vedaranyam march from Trichinopoly (13 April 1930); Kamaraj was first imprisoned in it.

new.s: Which leader was associated with the Chittagong armoury raid and a proclaimed provisional government?
new.x: Surya Sen led the Chittagong armoury raid and proclaimed a provisional government.

new.s: Rani Gaidinliu, arrested in 1932, led resistance in which region?
new.x: Rani Gaidinliu led the movement in the Manipur/Naga hills; Nehru called her "Rani".

new.s: Which of the following pairs (centre - region) is correctly matched?
new.x: Sanikatta was the Karnataka salt satyagraha centre; Dharasana is in Gujarat and Vedaranyam in Tamil Nadu.

new.s: During the CDM, protests against the Cunningham Circular took place in:
new.x: The Cunningham Circular protests were in Assam; the Chaukidari Tax agitation was in Bihar.

new.s: The Qissa Khwani firing of April 1930 took place at:
new.x: The Qissa Khwani firing (April 1930) was in Peshawar, during the Khudai Khidmatgar protests.

new.s: Babu Genu, a martyr of the Civil Disobedience Movement, died when:
o: He was crushed by a lorry carrying foreign cloth in Bombay
new.x: Babu Genu was crushed by a lorry carrying foreign cloth in Bombay on 12 December 1930 - not at Dharasana.

new.s: Khudiram Bose's Muzaffarpur bomb (1908) was aimed at:
new.x: Khudiram Bose targeted magistrate Kingsford in Muzaffarpur on 30 April 1908.

new.s: The Chapekar brothers shot plague commissioner W.C. Rand at Pune in:
new.x: The Chapekar brothers shot Rand in Pune in 1897 - the revolutionary phase, not the CDM.

new.s: Which of the following belongs to the Civil Disobedience Movement and NOT to the earlier revolutionary phase?
new.x: Babu Genu died in the CDM (1930); Khudiram, Prafulla Chaki and the Chapekars belong to 1897-1908.

new.s: In 1930, during the CDM, a textile workers' rising led to martial law at:
new.x: The Sholapur textile workers' rising in 1930 led to martial law.

new.s: Duvvuri Subbamma, a woman leader jailed in the CDM, belonged to which district of Andhra?
new.x: Duvvuri Subbamma was an East Godavari woman leader jailed in the CDM.

new.s: Aruna Asaf Ali is best known for hoisting the flag at Gowalia Tank during the:
new.x: Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank in 1942 (Quit India), not in the CDM.

new.s: Sarojini Naidu became the first Indian woman President of the INC at which session?
new.x: Sarojini Naidu presided over the Kanpur session of 1925.

new.s: Which Salt Satyagraha camp in Andhra was called the 'Dakshina Dandi'?
new.x: Devarampadu near Ongole, with its camp at Prakasam's house, was the Dakshina Dandi; Seethanagaram was the Andhra Dandi.

new.s: At Mylapadu in Nellore, salt was made on 11 April 1930 by:
new.x: Oruganti Venkatasubbayya and Bezawada Gopal Reddy made salt at Mylapadu, Nellore, on 11 April 1930.

new.s: Pedaganjam-Chinaganjam on the Andhra coast is famous for:
new.x: Pedaganjam-Chinaganjam is a famous salt-making coast (APPSC 2019).

new.s: Who led the first salt squad in Madras on 13 April 1930 along with Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao?
new.x: T. Prakasam and Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao led the first salt squad from the Swarajya office in Madras.

new.s: In the Chirala and Guntur villages, the CDM was led by Konda Venkatappayya and:
new.x: Konda Venkatappayya and Unnava Lakshminarayana led in Chirala and the Guntur villages.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT agreed to by Lord Irwin in the Gandhi-Irwin Pact?
o: Coastal villagers making salt for own use
Commuting the death sentences of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru
new.x: Irwin refused to commute the death sentences and refused a public inquiry into police excesses.

new.s: Who called Gandhi and Irwin the "Two Mahatmas"?
new.x: Sarojini Naidu called Gandhi and Irwin the "Two Mahatmas".

new.s: The First Round Table Conference (12 Nov 1930 - 19 Jan 1931) was:
new.x: The Congress boycotted the First RTC in London as the CDM was on.

new.s: What was the Congress position at the Third Round Table Conference (Nov-Dec 1932)?
new.x: The Congress did not attend the Third RTC; it attended only the Second.

new.s: The Communal Award granting separate electorates to the depressed classes was announced on:
new.x: The Communal Award came on 16 August 1932, before the Poona Pact of 24 September 1932.

new.s: The Poona Pact was signed on behalf of the caste Hindus by:
new.x: Ambedkar signed for the depressed classes and Madan Mohan Malaviya for the caste Hindus.

new.s: How many seats in provincial legislatures did the Poona Pact reserve for the depressed classes?
new.x: The Poona Pact gave 148 reserved seats against 71 under the Communal Award.

new.s: Who was the first president of the Harijan Sevak Sangh founded in 1932?
new.x: G.D. Birla was the first president and Thakkar Bapa the secretary of the Harijan Sevak Sangh.

new.s: The Harijan Sevak Sangh (30 September 1932) was first named:
new.x: It began as the Anti-Untouchability League, founded by Gandhi.

new.s: Gandhi's fast unto death against separate electorates for the depressed classes began on:
new.x: The Yerwada fast began on 20 September 1932, leading to the Poona Pact of 24 September.

new.s: Chandra Shekhar Azad's martyrdom (27 Feb 1931) came just before the:
new.x: Azad died on 27 February 1931; the Gandhi-Irwin Pact followed on 5 March 1931.

new.s: The first phase of the Civil Disobedience Movement ended with the:
new.x: The first phase ran 1930-31 up to the Gandhi-Irwin Pact; the second phase was 1932-34.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the significance of the Civil Disobedience Movement:
1. It was the first movement to break laws openly on a mass scale.
2. It brought the NWFP into the national movement.
3. Revolutionary activity merged into it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The CDM broke laws openly on a mass scale and drew in the NWFP; revolutionary activity stayed separate, so 3 is false.

new.s: The Pallepadu Ashram, a Civil Disobedience camp, was located in which district?
new.x: Pallepadu Ashram was the camp in Nellore district.

new.s: Vedavanam, Prakasam's house that served as a CDM camp, was located in:
new.x: Vedavanam was in Madras, not in Krishna district.

new.s: Who led the Salt Satyagraha at Vadarevu on the Guntur coast?
new.x: Kasi Viswanadham led at Vadarevu; Bulusu Sambamurthy led at Kakinada (Chollangi).

new.s: Dandu Narayana Raju led the Salt Satyagraha at:
new.x: APPSC 2023 key: Dandu Narayana Raju - Mattapalem.

new.s: Who led the Salt Satyagraha at Mylapadu beach in Nellore district?
new.x: Bezawada Gopal Reddy (with Bomma Seshareddy) led at Mylapadu, Nellore.

new.s: Ravi Narayana Reddy led the Salt Satyagraha at Ramachandrapuram in which district?
new.x: Ramachandrapuram, led by Ravi Narayana Reddy, is in East Godavari.

new.s: Who bought the auctioned salt during the Machilipatnam Salt Satyagraha?
new.x: Puranam Suri Sastry bought the auctioned salt at Machilipatnam.

new.s: Uppada on the Andhra coast is known for:
new.x: Uppada is known for Jamdani silk sarees; Kalamkari is Machilipatnam's and salt Pedaganjam-Chinaganjam's.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (centre - product) is correctly matched?
new.x: Machilipatnam is known for Kalamkari; Uppada for Jamdani and Pedaganjam-Chinaganjam for salt.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT part of the CDM programme in Andhra villages?
o: Picketing foreign-cloth shops in towns only
new.x: Making salt was itself part of the village programme; cutting palms and picketing were too, with foreign-cloth picketing in towns.

new.s: Volunteers from which institution joined the CDM in May 1930?
new.x: Eluru National School volunteers joined in May 1930.

new.s: A later anti-arrack agitation by women began in 1991 at:
new.x: Women launched the anti-arrack agitation at Dubagunta (Nellore) in 1991.

new.s: Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi was arrested in the Salt Satyagraha at:
new.x: She was arrested at Vedaranyam after Rajaji's arrest, on 15 May 1930.

new.s: Who carried the 'Swarajya Lakshmi Vratam' door to door on Ugadi in Guntur?
new.x: Unnava Lakshmibayamma ran the Swarajya Lakshmi Vratam on Ugadi in Guntur.

new.s: Which woman leader led women into the Salt Satyagraha?
new.x: Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay led women into the Salt Satyagraha.

new.s: Gandhi was arrested on the night of 4-5 May 1930 at:
new.x: Gandhi was arrested at Karadi near Dandi and taken to Yerwada Jail.

new.s: Webb Miller, who reported the Dharasana beatings, worked for:
new.x: Webb Miller was an American journalist of the United Press.

new.s: Who was the first declared leader of the Salt Satyagraha after Gandhi's arrest?
new.x: Abbas Tyabji was first (arrested 12 May 1930), then Sarojini Naidu.

new.s: Who led the Salt Satyagraha in Malabar (Kerala)?
new.x: K. Kelappan led in Malabar; Rajaji in Tamil Nadu.

new.s: Satish Chandra Dasgupta led the Salt Satyagraha in Bengal at:
new.x: Satish Chandra Dasgupta led at Mahishbathan in 24 Parganas.

new.s: Who led the Salt Satyagraha in Odisha (Balasore, Cuttack, Puri)?
new.x: Gopabandhu Chaudhuri led the Odisha salt satyagraha.

new.s: Which CDM volunteer was lathi-charged at Rajahmundry?
new.x: Venneti Satyanarayana was lathi-charged at Rajahmundry; Thota Narsayya at Machilipatnam.

new.s: The Berhampore firing during the repression of the CDM took place on:
new.x: The Berhampore firing was on 15 January 1932, under Lord Willingdon.

new.s: Thota Narsayya, known as 'Jenda Narsayya', had hoisted the flag at Machilipatnam on:
new.x: He hoisted the flag at Machilipatnam on 26 January 1930 and was later injured at Tilak Chowk.

new.s: Gandhi's letter of 2 March 1930 to Lord Irwin contained how many demands?
new.x: The letter to Irwin carried 11 demands, the main one being abolition of the salt tax.

new.s: In which year was the Civil Disobedience Movement finally withdrawn?
new.x: The second phase (1932-34) ended with the CDM withdrawn in 1934.

new.s: Gandhi reached Dandi on:
new.x: He reached Dandi on 5 April and broke the salt law on 6 April 1930.

new.s: Where were the Round Table Conferences held?
new.x: The British offered RTCs in London to frame a new constitution.

new.s: Why did the Congress stay away from the First Round Table Conference?
o: It had joined the Muslim League boycott
The Viceroy did not invite it
Lahore 1929 had said there was no benefit from the RTC
new.x: Lahore had declared no benefit from the RTC, and the CDM was in progress with leaders in jail.

new.s: The First Round Table Conference was inaugurated by:
new.x: King George V opened it; Ramsay MacDonald was its chairman.

new.s: Who chaired the First Round Table Conference?
new.x: British PM Ramsay MacDonald was the chairman.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the First Round Table Conference:
1. It began on 12 November 1930.
2. The Congress boycotted it.
3. Ambedkar attended it for the depressed classes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: It ran 12 Nov 1930 - 19 Jan 1931 without Congress; Ambedkar attended for the depressed classes.

new.s: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on:
new.x: The Delhi Pact was signed on 5 March 1931 - not March 1930.

new.s: Who mediated the Gandhi-Irwin Pact?
o: Tej Bahadur Sapru and M.R. Jayakar
new.x: Sapru and Jayakar (also V.S. Srinivasa Sastri) were the mediators.

new.s: Which of the following did Lord Irwin refuse in the Gandhi-Irwin Pact?
o: A public inquiry into police excesses
Salt-making for own use by coastal villagers
new.x: Irwin refused a public inquiry into police excesses and commutation of Bhagat Singh's sentence.

new.s: Under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact, the Congress agreed to:
o: Suspend the CDM and attend the 2nd RTC
new.x: Gandhi agreed to suspend the CDM and attend the Second RTC.

new.s: Who called Gandhi's gains in the Gandhi-Irwin Pact "Consolation Prizes"?
new.x: Irwin's biographer Alan Campbell Johnson used the phrase.

new.s: The Karachi session of the Congress was held on:
new.x: The Karachi session met on 29-31 March 1931, days after Bhagat Singh's execution on 23 March.

new.s: Nehru drafted the Karachi Fundamental Rights resolution with the help of:
new.x: Jawaharlal Nehru drafted it with M.N. Roy's help.

new.s: At the Second Round Table Conference, Sarojini Naidu represented:
new.x: Gandhi alone represented Congress; Sarojini Naidu represented Indian women.

new.s: Which leader did NOT go to the Second Round Table Conference?
new.x: Nehru did not go, as Gandhi alone represented Congress.

new.s: The Second Round Table Conference was held from:
new.x: RTC-2 met in London from 7 September to 1 December 1931.

new.s: Facing deadlock at the Second RTC, Ramsay MacDonald threatened:
new.x: MacDonald threatened a one-sided award, which became the Communal Award of 1932.

new.s: Which Viceroy 'struck first' when the CDM was resumed in January 1932?
new.x: Lord Willingdon arrested Gandhi, banned the Congress and issued ordinances.

new.s: The firing on satyagrahis at Berhampur took place on:
new.x: The Berhampur firing was on 15 January 1932, during the repression.

new.s: Gandhi was released from jail during the second phase of the CDM on:
new.x: Gandhi was released on 8 May 1933; mass CDM was suspended on 14 July 1933.

new.s: The Communal Award was announced by:
new.x: British PM Ramsay MacDonald announced it on 16 August 1932.

new.s: The Poona Pact was signed by:
new.x: Ambedkar (depressed classes) and Malaviya (caste Hindus) signed it; Gandhi did not sign.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Poona Pact:
1. It was signed at Yerwada Jail on 24 September 1932.
2. It retained separate electorates for the depressed classes.
3. It gave 148 reserved seats in provincial legislatures.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Pact dropped separate electorates for reserved seats in joint electorates - 148 against 71 under the Award.

new.s: The Third Round Table Conference was held in:
new.x: RTC-3 met from 17 November to 24 December 1932, without the Congress.

new.s: The Third Round Table Conference led to the White Paper of 1933 and then the:
new.x: White Paper (March 1933) - Joint Select Committee - Government of India Act, 1935.

new.s: Besides the Congress, which party also stayed away from the Third RTC?
new.x: Attendance was poor; the Labour Party too stayed away.

new.s: After the CDM was withdrawn, Congress returned to council entry and contested the Central Assembly elections in:
new.x: In 1934 Congress revived council entry and contested the Central Assembly elections.

new.s: After the CDM, which constructive work did Gandhi make his top priority?
new.x: Gandhi turned to constructive work, with "Service to Harijans" his top priority.

new.s: When was the Non-Cooperation Movement launched?
new.x: NCM began on 1 August 1920; Chauri Chaura was 4 Feb 1922.

new.s: The Swaraj Party was formed on:
new.x: The Swaraj Party came on 1 January 1923, after the NCM was withdrawn.

new.s:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Poona Pact
2. Chauri Chaura
3. Cripps Mission
4. Gandhi-Irwin Pact
new.x: Chauri Chaura (1922) - Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931) - Poona Pact (1932) - Cripps Mission (1942).

new.s: The Bardoli resolution by which the NCM was withdrawn was adopted in:
new.x: The Bardoli resolution of 11-12 February 1922 followed Chauri Chaura.
